title: Protocol for Creating Major Ion Solutions for Freshwater Systems
author: Malcolm A Barnard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bvyxn7xn
materials: from USGS data (Harned 1982). References: Harned, D.A.,

steps.title: Determine elemental concentrations
steps.instruction: Identify the elemental concentrations of Si 4+, Ca 2+, Mg 2+, Na+, K+, Cl-, and SO 4 2- in the target freshwater system.

steps.title: Convert concentration units
steps.instruction: Convert the elemental concentrations from µM to mg/L if they are not already in that format.

steps.title: Prepare calculation tool
steps.instruction: Download the 'Freshwater_Major_Ion_Solution_calculation.csv' file from Zenodo at http://www.doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5019969.

steps.title: Calculate salt requirements
steps.instruction: Use the downloaded CSV tool to determine the required mass of salts for the solution.

substeps.instruction: Enter the mg/L values calculated from the identification and conversion steps into the purple highlighted mg/L box.
Locate the required concentrations in the 'MIS Recipe' box at the bottom of the document (available for 5 L, 10 L, and 20 L volumes).

Verify that the final concentrations are not magnitudes off compared to the reference, specifically checking Na+, SO 4 2-, and Cl- concentrations. If values are several magnitudes off, use the values calculated using the anions.

steps.title: Prepare initial water volume
steps.instruction: Add approximately 1/20 of the total desired volume of distilled water to the intended container (e.g., use a 20 L carboy for a 20 L total volume).

substeps.instruction: Use graduated cylinders for volumetric measurements.

steps.title: Add salts to solution
steps.instruction: Add the calculated concentrations of the following salts to the distilled water in the container: Na 2 SiO 3 x9H 2 O, CaCl 2 x2H 2 O, MgSO 4 x7H 2 O, Na 2 SO 4, and K 2 SO 4.

steps.title: Finalize and mix solution
steps.instruction: Fill the container to the desired final volume using distilled water and mix until all salts are completely dissolved.
